name: Travel and Hospitality
title: Disruption-aware guest journey recovery
summary: Coordinate booking, inventory, accessibility requirements, and supplier policies before confirming a traveler-approved change.
situation: Illustrative architecture: A travel operator manages guests whose delayed arrival affects hotel check-in, airport transfers, and a prepaid activity. Service staff need compatible alternatives across suppliers. Agents prepare options with clear terms; travelers and authorized staff approve changes and financial commitments.
problem: Availability expires quickly, supplier confirmation can lag, and one successful cancellation may leave another service unchanged. An agent that says the journey is fixed after a single receipt can leave the guest stranded or double booked.
whyAgents: Booking, inventory, policy, and itinerary specialists work on separate supplier interfaces. A durable coordinator owns reservation expiry, customer consent, and partial-success recovery across the journey.
outcome: The intended result is a reviewable operational decision with source evidence and explicit ownership. Evaluate confirmed recovery quality and repeat contacts alongside preparation time. Guest satisfaction depends on supplier execution and individual needs, so retain requirement-level evidence and unresolved obligations throughout the case.

agents.name: Booking reconciler
agents.responsibility: Read confirmed itinerary items, traveler entitlements, and prior change operations.
agents.boundary: Cannot cancel or change bookings without scoped approval.

agents.name: Alternative finder
agents.responsibility: Query current rooms, transfers, and activity options matching recorded requirements.
agents.boundary: Cannot assume accessibility from marketing text or promise unheld inventory.

agents.name: Policy evidence agent
agents.responsibility: Retrieve change terms and calculate supplier-confirmed charges.
agents.boundary: Cannot waive supplier conditions or invent refund eligibility.

agents.name: Journey coordinator
agents.responsibility: Present compatible options and manage the approved change sequence.
agents.boundary: Requires traveler consent for the exact itinerary and authorized approval for exceptions.

systems.name: Reservation and customer platforms
systems.role: Own confirmed bookings, traveler identity, preferences, and approved communication.

systems.name: Supplier distribution adapters
systems.role: Expose live availability, temporary holds, confirmation receipts, and cancellation status.

systems.name: Payment and service recovery systems
systems.role: Track charges, refunds, vouchers, and unresolved partial changes independently.

flow.title: Register disruption
flow.description: Verify traveler identity and link affected itinerary components with current confirmations and remaining service deadlines.

flow.title: Read constraints
flow.description: Retrieve explicit accessibility, timing, occupancy, and change-policy requirements without inferring sensitive preferences.

flow.title: Find compatible options
flow.description: Query suppliers in parallel and label unheld quotes, held inventory, and confirmed bookings distinctly.

flow.title: Price complete change
flow.description: Calculate total fees and refund timing across components, including the consequences if only part of the plan succeeds.

flow.title: Confirm traveler choice
flow.description: Present exact services, times, accessibility confirmations, amounts, and expiry before recording consent.

flow.title: Execute coordinated recovery
flow.description: Commit held components in the approved order, reconcile acknowledgements, and escalate or compensate partial changes under the agreed policy.

diagrams.title: Failure and decision sequence
diagrams.code:
sequenceDiagram
    participant O as "Case orchestrator"
    participant S as "Reservation and customer platforms"
    participant H as "Accountable reviewer"
O->>S: Read confirmed journey components
    O->>H: Present complete priced change
    H-->>O: Approve itinerary and limits
    O->>S: Commit held components
    S-->>O: Transfer confirmed and hotel rejected
    O->>H: Present partial recovery and next options
diagrams.caption: A hotel hold expires while the transfer change succeeds. The workflow records unresolved work and resumes only after the source state and reviewer authority are checked.

failures.scenario: A hotel hold expires while the transfer change succeeds.
failures.detection: Supplier receipts show a confirmed transfer but rejected accommodation commitment.
failures.recovery: Keep the case open, present remaining options, and apply only the compensation actions the traveler approved.

failures.detection: Supplier data lacks the required confirmed attribute or conflicts with the guest's requirement.
failures.recovery: Request supplier confirmation and exclude the option from confirmed-compatible choices until resolved.

controls: Require traveler consent bound to exact itinerary components, prices, and change terms.
Keep accessibility requirements explicit and verify supplier evidence before making commitments.
Protect passport and identity data from unnecessary specialist prompts and logs.
Track each supplier operation with its own idempotency key and confirmation state.
Never describe a partially completed journey change as fully confirmed.

metrics.name: Compatible option latency
metrics.definition: Time from verified disruption to a fully priced option satisfying recorded requirements.

metrics.name: Confirmation completeness
metrics.definition: Approved changes with all required supplier receipts divided by approved changes.

metrics.name: Partial recovery duration
metrics.definition: Time from first partial failure to traveler-accepted resolution or accountable escalation.

metrics.name: Requirement fidelity
metrics.definition: Audited booked options meeting all explicitly recorded requirements divided by audited booked options.

tradeoffs.cost: Introduces distributed transaction and compensation complexity.
May incur fees or consume scarce capacity until released.

tradeoffs.benefit: Protects traveler needs from vague recommendations.
tradeoffs.cost: Supplier metadata gaps can reduce available options.

rollout.acceptance: Service staff verify consent, pricing, accessibility evidence, and partial booking recovery.
One destination team reviews options without supplier mutations or customer promises.
Selected suppliers launch after hold-expiry, duplicate-payment, and partial-confirmation tests pass.
